Domik is a free, unofficial, open source educational project (MIT licence) for controlling a 1st-generation Deimic controller on your home network.

• This is not an official Deimic app or a replacement for it. The manufacturer is not affiliated with it, does not approve it and does not support it.

• Your data stays with you. The author receives no data. The app controls your controller on your network, without any cloud. The Open-Meteo weather service receives only the place name you type and its approximate location. If you add the optional eModul integration yourself, the app sends your API key to the eModul service of TECH Sterowniki and only reads your controllers' data – that is an independent service the author is not responsible for.

• Use at your own risk, without warranty. Bugs can happen, and the status on screen may differ from reality.

• Don't rely on it for safety. Frost protection, pumps, heating and blinds must work without the app too. A command may not reach the controller, e.g. without a network or if the tablet switches off. Keep your wall switches and existing controls.

• Only control your own installation – or someone else's with the owner's permission.

• The serial number is the key to your home. Anyone who knows it and is on your network can control the installation. Never share it – including in reports on GitHub.

• Download the app only from the official source: github.com/milwis/domik/releases.

This is a summary. The Terms of Use and Privacy Policy apply: github.com/milwis/domik/tree/main/legal. Your statutory consumer rights are not affected. Contact the author: github.com/milwis/domik/issues.

Domik will send the installer calibration for this room\u2019s sensor to the controller (command 0x132 – a change to the controller configuration). The controller\u2019s temperature reading returns to the value from before Domik\u2019s correction, and heating control and Deimic displays start using it. When the difference from the thermometer exceeds the threshold again, Domik may correct the calibration again.
Test mode: nothing will be sent to the controller. Only a log entry about restoring the installer calibration will be added.
Domik compares the room thermometers with the Deimic sensors. Turning it off in live mode restores the installer calibration.
Only one device (e.g. the wall tablet) should receive thermometers and send calibrations. Turning it on asks for Bluetooth and notification permission.
Decisions only go to the log – they show how often the calibration would be changed.
Writing calibrations is turned off in this version of the app.

Domik will send new sensor calibrations to the controller (command 0x132) – this changes the controller configuration. A calibration changes the temperature reading the controller uses to regulate heating and that Deimic displays show; it stays in the controller\u2019s memory even after a power loss. The installer calibration is remembered and can be restored at any time.
The calibration is changed when the average difference between the thermometer and the Deimic sensor exceeds the threshold. The log counts changes for both thresholds.

Show selected readings from your TECH boiler and controllers (eModul) on the dashboard: temperatures, valves, fuel. Domik only reads data – it changes nothing on the controller.

Domik will connect to the eModul service of TECH Sterowniki (emodul.eu), sending your API key, and will fetch your controllers\' data about once a minute while the dashboard is open. The key is encrypted on this device. Domik changes nothing on the controller. By pressing "Next" you agree to this connection. Details: privacy policy, section 4(5) (github.com/milwis/domik/blob/main/legal/polityka-prywatnosci.md).
Generate the key in eModul: Settings → Account → at the very bottom "Generate API key". Copy it and paste it below.
